class.name: TerrainSlopeLayer
class.brief_description: A terrain material placed by steepness rather than climate.
class.description: A material painted on top of the biome blend wherever the ground is steep enough, typically rock or cliff. Unlike [TerrainBiomeLayer], it ignores climate entirely and is driven only by surface normal, so it reads as exposed bedrock. Assign it to [member TerrainConfiguration.rock_layer] to use it as the default rock for every biome, or to [member TerrainBiomeLayer.slope_layer] to give one biome cliffs of its own. Layers are deduplicated by texture set, so sharing one across many biomes costs a single slice of GPU memory. [b]How steepness is measured.[/b] Slope is [code]1.0 - dot(normal, UP)[/code], so [code]0.0[/code] is dead flat and [code]1.0[/code] is a vertical wall. It is not an angle and not linear in one: roughly [code]0.1[/code] is a 26° slope, [code]0.3[/code] is 45°, and the default [code]0.6[/code] is about 66°. [b]If the layer never shows up[/b], that is almost always the reason: [member slope_threshold] sits above the steepest slope the terrain actually produces. Terrain steepness is set by [member TerrainConfiguration.height_scale] against [member TerrainConfiguration.noise_base_frequency], and gentle settings simply never reach 66°. The threshold has to fall below roughly the terrain's 95th-percentile slope for the layer to appear on more than a stray pixel, so either lower it, or raise [member TerrainConfiguration.height_scale]. Emits [signal Resource.changed], so edits update the terrain live.

members.member: Base colour texture for this layer. Without it the layer contributes no visible material.
Ambient occlusion map, multiplied into the layer's indirect lighting.
Height (displacement) map driving parallax occlusion mapping. Only used when [member pom_depth] is above zero.
Tangent-space normal map, in OpenGL convention (green channel pointing up).

Depth of the parallax occlusion effect, in UV-space units. [code]0.0[/code] disables parallax for this layer entirely, which is the cheapest option and the right one for layers with no [member height_texture]. Small values read as surface texture; large ones make silhouettes swim at grazing angles. Step counts and distance fade are shared across layers and set on [TerrainConfiguration] under [b]Parallax[/b]. Range [code]0.0[/code] to [code]0.25[/code], and it accepts larger values.
Roughness map. Read from the red channel; white is fully rough, black is mirror-smooth.

Half-width of the smoothstep either side of [member slope_threshold]. The layer fades in from [code]threshold - range[/code] and is fully opaque by [code]threshold + range[/code]. Do not drive this toward zero to get a crisp rock line. Slope is view-independent but the transition it produces is not perceptually stable at a hard edge: a near-zero blend range makes the boundary alias and appear to crawl as the camera moves. Keep it wide enough to cover a few pixels of slope variation. Range [code]0.01[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. Clamped to a minimum of [code]0.001[/code] in the shader.

Steepness at which this layer reaches half coverage, as [code]1.0 - dot(normal, UP)[/code], [code]0.0[/code] is flat, [code]1.0[/code] is vertical. The default [code]0.6[/code] is roughly a 66° slope, which gentle terrain never reaches; see the class description if the layer is not showing up. Range [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code].

How many times the layer's textures repeat per world unit. Lower values stretch the texture over more ground; higher values tile it more tightly and show tiling artifacts sooner. Range [code]0.001[/code] to [code]2.0[/code], and it accepts larger values.
